title: Caring for perineal stitches after birth
what: After birth, you may have stitches in the perineum, the area between the vagina and the anus. Simple care helps them heal faster.
why: If you had a tear or a cut in the perineum during birth.
duration: stitches usually heal in 2 to 3 weeks; dissolving stitches go away on their own
tell_doctor: If the pain gets worse instead of better
If there is a bad smell or pus
If it is hard to pee or have a bowel movement

prepare.title: Hygiene
prepare.text: Rinse with warm water after every trip to the toilet, front to back.

prepare.title: Pads
prepare.text: Change your pad often, usually every 2 to 4 hours.

prepare.title: Drying
prepare.text: Pat the stitches dry with a clean towel. Do not rub.

bring: A separate towel for the area
steps: Wash your hands before caring for the stitches
Rinse with warm water from front to back
Gently pat dry with a towel
If a product was prescribed, apply it as your doctor said
At first, sit carefully, on one side or on a soft cushion, unless your doctor says otherwise
feel: For the first few days, the stitches ache and pull
It may sting when you pee. Pouring warm water over the area helps
after: Try not to strain on the toilet, and drink more water
The doctor will check the stitches at your visit
Sex is usually put off until your doctor says it is OK
red_flags: Severe pain, swelling, or pus around the stitches

faq.a: Usually you can sit carefully right away, but your doctor will tell you more. A soft cushion helps.

faq.q: Do the stitches need to be removed?
faq.a: Usually the stitches dissolve on their own. If not, the doctor will tell you when to come.

reminders.text: How are your stitches healing? Rinse after using the toilet and change your pad often.
